scope: Instrumentation-only repetition of frozen first state; original V37 scores are authoritative.

findings.evidence: Across the 148 original banks, continuations use 66.132 of 67.892 CPU seconds; 44,420 cold ride and 34,844 cold platform compiles remain after caching.
findings.action: Optimize the continuation planner; sampling, trace recording and snapshot copying are not the main target.

findings.evidence: The first-state profile calls clock_nominal_score 32,715 times, consuming 0.100 instrumented seconds including scalar score/interp.
findings.action: Compute scores for a clock vector in one interpolation call, or reuse board_scores at the identical grid; retain the existing off-grid projection, support checks and FullMenuOpportunity integer-clock semantics.

findings.component: Unrequested stopping policies and terminal chains
findings.evidence: The first-state profile calls OnboardStopping.solve 472 times (0.061 instrumented seconds), generating optimal, rolling and rollout policies although execution requests only rolling_fixed. A one-exit destination ride also takes this path.
findings.action: Provide the mathematically identical rolling_fixed recursion and one-exit terminal result directly; do not remove deadline/killed mass or current public arrival masks.

findings.evidence: conditional_action_check constructs a fresh ForecastPlanner inside each action loop; existing keys already include node structure, method and relevant trip evidence.
findings.action: Share the immutable planner cache across both arms of the same frozen bank. This is a code-proven duplicate-cache opportunity; the current profile does not measure the arm-key intersection or its speed gain.

findings.evidence: MessageHistory.law uses 0.156 instrumented seconds; 408 departure_evidence calls use 0.120 seconds. These are nested timings, not additive.
findings.action: A shared cache may reuse an exactly equal ordered trip history and active emission; preserve observation order and off-grid projection. First measure the simpler planner changes.

findings.evidence: 699 record calls use 0.000331 seconds; 257 full history clone calls use 0.003419 seconds.
findings.action: Retain public traces and independent histories; removing them cannot address the measured bottleneck.

limitations: The cProfile timings include instrumentation and cover one predeclared state. Cumulative function times overlap. No full-bank speedup or new scientific outcome is claimed; the 128-world value remains a finite-bank value, not an exact population expectation.
